messages:
maya: Quick sync — postmortem found policy chose a 15% cheaper variant in the same region even though its p99 jumped. Result: frontend retry storm and customer SLA breach. Need a hardened signal contract.

sam: Agree. Root cause: runtime didn't include any health hint, policy only had cost and model-compat. We fell back on cost as tie-break.

alex: We discussed in the RFC but didn't lock a rollout plan. Proposal: 1) define three canonical runtime fields (capacity_score, steady_p99_ms, signal_ts); 2) treat capacity_score < 0.5 as "unsafe" for cost-preference; 3) add explicit hedging window.

eli: One more: we should separate probe-derived metrics from aggregate observability. Runtimes should publish the probe p99 (fast window) and the aggregated p99 (1m). Policy should prefer probe when deciding immediate hedges but use aggregate for telemetry.

jordan: TTLs are crucial. If signal_ts is > 10s old, degrade capacity_score toward 0.2 exponentially. Otherwise stale probes mask hot GPUs during bursts.

rachel: UX ask: in Console show the normalized signal alongside the raw metric so SREs can validate mappings. Also expose per-tenant opt-in for cost-aggressive mode.

sam: Implementation sketch (policy-compiler adapter): normalize signals -> apply staleness aging -> compute safety_flag = capacity_score >= 0.6 and steady_p99_ms <= 350 -> if safety_flag true, allow cost-based selection up to cost_delta_threshold; else trigger hedging.

maya: Pseudocode for clarity:
```
normalized = adapter.normalize(runtime_payload)
age = now - normalized.signal_ts
if age > 10s:
  normalized.capacity_score *= exp(-0.1 * (age-10)) // age penalty
safety = normalized.capacity_score >= 0.6 && normalized.steady_p99_ms <= 350
if safety:
  select by cost if cost_delta <= 0.2
else:
  hedge(to: N+1, prefer: latency, cost_cap: 0.33)
```

alex: Rollout plan: adapter in compiler can apply per-runtime mappers so we can ship adapter without runtime changes. Then change consoles/SDKs to document canonical fields and invite runtime owners to emit them.

eli: Testing: three sim suites: (A) probe-staleness scenario; (B) sudden p99 spike with cost delta; (C) slow cross-region egress increase. Need sim metrics: per-request latency, egress bytes, hedge_count, cost_delta.

jordan: Ops alerts to add: region.mean_capacity_score drop, hedge_rate spike, and per-tenant cost_overrun from hedging.

rachel: Also add a tenant-visible banner during opt-in that warns about potential egress. Decision needs to be transparent.

sam: Backwards compatibility: runtimes that don't emit fields get: capacity_score=0.35, steady_p99_ms=9999, signal_ts=now-60s. That forces conservative behavior. Make this explicit in SDK.

maya: Concern: some legacy runtimes are measured by an external probe that reports aggregate p99 only every 60s. Adapter heuristics must map that into steady_p99_ms and set signal_ts accordingly.

alex: Ops note: hedging increases cross-region traffic; Optimize team must add a per-tenant sim that estimates expected egress delta and cost. If cost delta > tenant-guardrail, policy should allow opt-out.

ops-bot: @alex created alert: "routing.hedge_rate_spike" threshold=10rps sustained 30s. Runbook linked.

deploy-bot: Canary image pushed: redwood/policy-compiler:feature-signal-contract-20260324.

eli: Action owners & ETA:
- eli: canonical field doc + adapter mapping table (ETA: Wed)
- sam: unit tests + sim job (ETA: Thu)
- maya: RFC follow-up PR with rollout notes (ETA: Tue)
- rachel: Console preview mock + opt-in UX copy (ETA: Mon)
- alex: coordinate Optimize sim and tenant guardrail (ETA: Fri)

maya: If no objections, I'll mark this RFC follow-up as accepted and start the rollout track. :+1:

sam: No objections from me.

rachel: :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks folks. We'll keep the per-tenant opt-in for 2 weeks while sims run.
